title: Jumping Flash! 2
subtitle: Robbit looks down on another world

body: Jumping Flash! 2 is Exact and MuuMuu's PlayStation platform game, first released in Japan on 26 April 1996. The robotic rabbit Robbit searches for MuuMuus scattered across large three-dimensional stages by Captain Kabuki. As in the original, the player sees through Robbit's eyes, using enormous jumps to explore structures from above. Height becomes a practical way to understand a level. An object difficult to locate from the ground can reveal itself during the ascent, turning the next landing into a decision made while the player is still far above it.

Robbit's triple jump gives access to distant platforms and high vantage points. The player studies the ground while airborne, choosing where to land and which part of the stage to investigate next. A meter makes the availability of that jump clearer, while a longer draw distance helps more of the world remain visible. These refinements support the original's unusual relationship between movement and observation. The player is not simply crossing a gap: each ascent offers another chance to assemble a useful picture of the places and targets spread below.

Koji Tada directed the sequel, with Takeo Miratsu returning to compose its music. Much of the earlier interface was retained, allowing development to focus on new worlds and improvements to the existing play. Reviews welcomed the graphics and handling while questioning the short length and close resemblance to the first game. North American and British editions followed later in 1996. The sequel demonstrates how distinctive the original idea already was, developing a first-person platform game around the pleasure of rising above a landscape and choosing a route back down.
